title: Data contract drift and isolated dbt fixture verification
summary: Implement separate structural and actual data quality checks with approved contract pins and host-owned dbt DuckDB fixture evidence.
problemStatement: Existing Runtime runners have no data-contract compatibility model or dbt fixture evidence adapter.

inScope: Runtime-private data contract and directional drift checking
Host-owned dbt Core DuckDB fixture runner and QualityGate adapter
Standard-role skills through P28 ownership review
outOfScope: Real warehouse access or destructive migrations
CLI command/config wiring without CLI-owner review
Public contract changes and live-provider/Herdr acceptance

acceptanceCriteria.description: Validate accepted contract revision, digest and matching approval; block stale pins
Classify field removal, rename, type, nullability, key and schema evolution per consumer direction
Reject missing required tests and unapproved threshold changes
Separate structural and data quality outcomes and reject malformed or incomplete reports
Run real dbt Core and DuckDB on isolated passing and violating fixtures with provenance
Measure required null, unique, referential integrity and accepted values checks
Block prerequisite gaps and uncertain termination, clean only owned resources
Use standard roles in data pipeline, dbt and contract skills and document adapter limits
Run repository validation and report exact results without committing or external writes

architectureNotes: See data-verification-design.md. Strict Runtime-private Zod models; existing exported contracts govern approvals, gates and trusted artifact ingress. Independent static and runtime outcomes.
dataModelChanges: Additive private fixture data models only; no existing database, journal or public contract migration.
securityConsiderations: Execute only host templates and safe fixture data against an owned temporary DuckDB database; no warehouse credentials, arbitrary candidate macros/hooks or outside cleanup.
rollbackPlan: Remove opt-in Runtime adapter and P28 skills; no persistence migration or production-resource rollback is necessary.

tddDecision.rationale: Directional compatibility, approval pins and evidence parsing are deterministic domain logic with reproducible failure cases.
verifiableConditions: Observe failing structural and report tests before implementation
Observe real dbt fixture pass and real data violation without synthetic runtime evidence

sdd.proposedTestStrategy: Conditional TDD required for deterministic domain logic; actual dbt subprocess fixtures for quality outcomes; catalog/schema checks and independent review for skills.
technicalConstraints: No shared contracts, root config, lockfile or docs edits
No commit, push, PR, real warehouse write or destructive migration
apiDataContracts: Existing @bflow/contracts approval, specification, gate and artifact schemas at package boundaries
New data models remain private to Runtime
risksAndTradeoffs: Fixture-only checks do not execute arbitrary candidate model SQL
CLI/daemon configuration integration deferred to owning agent
Missing tools/sandbox remains a prerequisite gap
sdd.migrationStrategy: No existing persistent schema changes. Additive private opt-in adapter only.
